1.explanation:
1. We add a new story called `ReadOnly` in `ComboBox.stories.js` so designers and devs can preview the behavior.
2. We pass the boolean `readOnly` prop (not supported yet) to the ComboBox. Under the hood it should:  
   • Render the <input> with the native `readonly` attribute.  
   • Apply the `.bx--combo-box--readonly` CSS class (matching text-secondary, placeholder, icon-disabled tokens).  
   • Still allow clicking on the clear (×) and toggle (▼) icons to open/clear.  
3. Running Storybook will reproduce the screenshot: a non-editable filter input showing the placeholder and selected value in read-only styling.
1.bug_scenario: The design requires a new read-only state for the Carbon ComboBox: the user should not be able to type into the input (it gains the native readonly attribute and “read-only” styling tokens), but they can still open the menu and clear the selection using the icons (both icons should be rendered in their disabled color tokens). In the screenshots we see the “Filter…” placeholder in a read-only ComboBox, and a preselected item (“Option 3”) also rendered in its read-only style.
